items.title: AI may not improve patient outcomes for stroke
items.excerpt: RSNA 2026 preview: Northwell/Hofstra compared 876 acute ischemic stroke patients before and after five AI tools went live at a comprehensive stroke center; after propensity matching, AI did not change odds of good functional outcome or discharge disposition, though CTA-within-60-minutes rose sharply.
items.rationale: Before/after real-world study at a stroke center: AI sped up imaging workflow but did not move patient functional outcomes, a direct check on what deployed stroke AI actually buys clinicians.

items.title: DL model cuts patient gadolinium exposure to 10% of standard dose
items.excerpt: RSNA 2026 preview: Subtle Medical's deep-learning algorithm restored brain MRI contrast enhancement from a 10% gadolinium dose; in 63 patients, blinded randomized reads found no significant difference in lesion categorization vs. standard-dose images.
items.rationale: Patient-facing safety gain: blinded randomized reads show brain MRI at 10% gadolinium dose with DL enhancement matches standard-dose lesion categorization.

items.title: Tele-Cranio: a CT-free AI solution for remote diagnosis and planning of craniomaxillofacial deformities
items.excerpt: npj Digital Medicine: Tele-Cranio is an AI system that enables remote, CT-free assessment and surgical planning for craniomaxillofacial deformities, cutting repeated in-hospital CT and radiation burden, particularly for children.
items.rationale: Remote, CT-free assessment and surgical planning for craniofacial deformities; reduces radiation and hospital visits for children, a telemedicine use not covered before.

items.title: Domain-specific large language models with chain-of-thought prompting for antibiotic prescribing: a 2x2 factorial evaluation
items.excerpt: BMJ Health & Care Informatics: compares a domain-specific medical LLM with a general-purpose LLM, with and without chain-of-thought prompting, on how rational and safe their antibiotic prescribing decisions are, plus an LLM-based auto-scorer.
items.rationale: Clinician-facing safety evidence on whether medical-domain LLMs and chain-of-thought prompting make antibiotic prescribing advice more rational and safe.

items.title: Development and validation of a machine learning model to predict outpatient appointment non-attendance: a retrospective study using multisource NHS data
items.excerpt: BMJ Open: an appointment-level ML model built on multisource NHS records predicts outpatient 'did not attend' risk to enable targeted interventions that reduce missed appointments.
items.rationale: Care-operations AI on real NHS data: flags patients likely to miss outpatient appointments so clinics can target reminders and reduce wasted slots.
